368969.title: The 3-edge-cut congruence for Speyer's polynomial
368969.statement:
Let $G$ be a $3$-vertex-connected graph with a $3$-edge cut $C$, so that deleting $C$ gives two connected components $S\sqcup T$. Let $A=G/T$ and $B=G/S$ be obtained by contracting one side of the cut, replacing it by a $3$-valent vertex.

**3-edge-cut conjecture.** The Speyer polynomials satisfy

$$
g_G(t)\equiv\frac{g_A(t)g_B(t)}{t}\pmod{t^3\mathbb{Z}[t]}.
$$

The congruence determines the linear and quadratic terms of $g_G(t)$ from the two contracted graphs. The paper reports confirmation for all tested cuts, while higher coefficients are explicitly shown not to be determined in general.

369161.title: Equality of the B-Z constants for powers of cycles and paths
369161.statement: Let $\mathcal{C}_k$ and $\mathcal{P}_k$ denote the graph families of $k$-th powers of cycles and paths, respectively, and let their B-Z constants be defined. **B-Z constant equality conjecture.** The B-Z constants of $\mathcal{C}_k$ and $\mathcal{P}_k$ are equal for all $k\ge 1$. This conjecture proposes that these two infinite graph families have identical exponential spanning-tree growth rates despite their different boundary structures; the supplied text does not indicate whether it has been resolved.

369162.title: Bounded-edge-deletion invariance of the B-Z constant
369162.statement:
Let $\mathcal{G}:=\{G_n\}_n$ and $\mathcal{H}:=\{H_n\}_n$ be indexed families of connected graphs, and suppose that the B-Z constants $BZ(\mathcal{G})$ and $BZ(\mathcal{H})$ both exist. Assume that

$$
H_n\subseteq G_n\quad\text{for all }n
$$

and that there is a constant $c_1$ such that

$$
\lvert E(G_n\setminus H_n)\rvert\leq c_1\quad\text{for all }n.
$$

**Bounded-edge-deletion invariance conjecture.** Under these assumptions, $\mathcal{G}$ and $\mathcal{H}$ have the same B-Z constant. The source explicitly marks this proposed statement as false, so it is refuted rather than open; grid and torus graph families provide the surrounding motivation and indicate that bounded modifications do not generally preserve the B-Z constant.

369258.title: CFG+Y characterization of polynomial 3-uniform Ramsey growth
369258.statement:
Let $H$ be a $3$-uniform hypergraph, let $K_n^3$ be the complete $3$-uniform hypergraph on $n$ vertices, and let $r(H,K_n^3)$ be the corresponding Ramsey number. Call $H$ **iterated tripartite** if it belongs to the iterated-tripartite class described in the source. **CFG+Y conjecture.** For any $3$-graph $H$, there is a constant $c$ such that

$$
r(H,K_n^3)\leq n^c
$$

for all $n$ if and only if $H$ is iterated tripartite. The source describes this as an adjacent open problem and as a strengthening of the paper's main theorem.

369318.title: The bounded-error conjecture for equitable matroid partitions
369318.statement:
Let $\mathcal{M}=(E,\mathcal{I})$ be a matroid whose ground set $E$ can be partitioned into $k$ disjoint bases, and let $S_1,S_2,\ldots,S_\ell$ be pairwise disjoint subsets of $E$. **Bounded-error equitable partition conjecture.** There exists a function $f\,:\,\mathbb{N}\to\mathbb{N}$ such that there is a partition of $E$ into $k$ disjoint bases $B_1,\ldots,B_k$ satisfying

$$
\left||B_i\cap S_j|-|S_j|/k\right|\le f(\ell)
$$

for all $i\in [k]$ and $j\in[\ell]$. This conjecture asks whether the discrepancy can be bounded solely in terms of the number of distinguished subsets, independently of the matroid, $k$, and their sizes.

369511.title: The sunflowerability conjecture for generic $K_n$-free graphs
369511.statement:
For each integer $n\geq 3$, let ${\mathcal{H}}_n$ be the countable generic $K_n$-free graph.

**The sunflowerability conjecture for generic $K_n$-free graphs.** For all $n\geq 3$, ${\mathcal{H}}_n$ is sunflowerable.

The paper recalls that ${\mathcal{H}}_n$ is ultrahomogeneous and indivisible, and proposes sunflowerability as a further property. Whether every countable generic $K_n$-free graph is sunflowerable remains open.

369595.title: The edge-redundant rigidity conjecture for complete graphs in $\ell_\infty^d$
369595.statement:
Let $d\geq 2$, let $n\geq 2d+2$, and let $K_n$ denote the complete graph on $n$ vertices. A graph is **edge-redundantly rigid** in a normed space if it has a framework that is infinitesimally rigid and remains infinitesimally rigid after deleting any edge. **Edge-redundant rigidity conjecture.** For every $d\geq 2$ and every $n\geq 2d+2$, the complete graph $K_n$ is edge-redundantly rigid in $\ell_\infty^d$.

The preceding proposition rules out $K_{2d+1}$, so the conjecture asserts that the stated threshold is sufficient as well as necessary. The supplied excerpt gives no evidence that the conjecture has been resolved.

369645.title: The cycle-free chromatic discrepancy conjecture
369645.statement:
Let $G$ be a graph. For an integer $\ell\ge 2$, call $G$ **$C_{\ell+1}$-free** if it contains no cycle of length exactly $\ell+1$ as a, not necessarily induced, subgraph. Let $\varphi(G)$ denote the chromatic discrepancy of $G$.

**Cycle-free chromatic discrepancy conjecture.** For every integer $\ell\ge 2$, every $C_{\ell+1}$-free graph $G$ satisfies

$$
\varphi(G)\ge \chi(G)-\ell.
$$

This is proposed as a weaker version of the locally $s$-colourable conjecture, because every $C_{\ell+1}$-free graph is locally $\ell$-colourable. The source explicitly states that this weaker form is open.

369646.title: The strengthened cycle-free chromatic discrepancy conjecture
369646.statement:
Let $G$ be a graph. For an integer $\ell\ge 3$, call $G$ **$C_{\ell+1}$-free** if it contains no cycle of length exactly $\ell+1$ as a, not necessarily induced, subgraph. Let $K_{\ell}$ denote the complete graph on $\ell$ vertices, and let $\varphi(G)$ denote the chromatic discrepancy of $G$.

**Strengthened cycle-free chromatic discrepancy conjecture.** For every integer $\ell\ge 3$, every $C_{\ell+1}$-free graph $G\ne K_{\ell}$ satisfies

$$
\varphi(G)\ge \chi(G)-\ell+1.
$$

The source presents this as a stronger conjecture motivated by the suspicion that equality in the weaker bound occurs only when $\ell=2$ or when $G$ is complete. Its status is not otherwise resolved in the supplied text.

369767.title: Quadratic Rado conjecture for homogeneous three-variable equations
369767.statement:
Let $a,b,c\in\mathbb{N}$. A **Rado triple** is a triple $(a,b,c)$ such that $a=c$, $b=c$, or $a+b=c$. An equation is **partition regular** if every finite partition of $\mathbb{N}$ contains distinct $x,y,z$ in one cell satisfying it.

**Quadratic Rado conjecture.** The equation

$$
a x^2+b y^2=c z^2
$$

is partition regular if and only if $(a,b,c)$ is a Rado triple.

This extends the classical linear classification of partition-regular equations to homogeneous quadratic equations. It includes the long-standing question of whether the Pythagorean equation is partition regular, and its general validity remains open.

370191.title: The rainbow tree conjecture for properly coloured regular graphs
370191.statement:
Let $G$ be a properly coloured $d$-regular graph, meaning that the edges incident with each vertex have distinct colours. A copy is **rainbow** if all its edges have distinct colours.

**Rainbow tree conjecture.** For every tree $T$ on $d$ vertices, every properly coloured $d$-regular graph $G$ contains a rainbow copy of $T$.

This conjecture generalises the rainbow path problem from complete graphs to regular graphs and trees. The paper leaves it as an open direction, while proving related results for Cayley-sum colourings.

370475.title: Refinement of Bezdek's conjecture for Larman points
370475.statement: Let $K\subset \mathbb{R}^{n}$ be a convex body with $n\geq 3$, and let $p\in\operatorname*{int}K$. For every hyperplane $\Pi$ passing through $p$, suppose the section $\Pi\cap K$ has an $(n-2)$-plane of symmetry; then $p$ is a **Larman point** of $K$. If, moreover, every such section has an $(n-2)$-plane of symmetry containing $p$, then $p$ is a **revolution point** of $K$. **Refinement of Bezdek's conjecture.** Suppose that $p$ is a Larman point of $K$ which is not a revolution point of $K$. Then either $K$ is an ellipsoid or $K$ is a body of revolution. This refinement concerns the global shape forced by the distinction between Larman and revolution points; the supplied source gives no resolution status.

370483.title: Four remaining 2-adic congruences for overpartition tuples with odd parts
370483.statement:
Let $\overline{OPT}_k(n)$ denote the number of overpartition $k$-tuples of $n$ with odd parts. **The four-congruence conjecture.** For all $i\geq 1$, $n\geq 0$, and odd $r>0$, 

$$
\begin{aligned}
\overline{OPT}_{2^i r}(8n+2)&\equiv 0 \pmod{2^{2i+1}},\\
\overline{OPT}_{2^i r}(8n+4)&\equiv 0 \pmod{2^{2i+4}},\\
\overline{OPT}_{2^i r}(8n+6)&\equiv 0 \pmod{2^{2i+3}},\\
\overline{OPT}_{2^i r}(8n+7)&\equiv 0 \pmod{2^{i+4}}.
\end{aligned}
$$

These are the four remaining congruences from a previously proposed set of seven; the source states that they have not been proved, so their general validity remains open.

370688.title: Switch-generation conjecture for the matching preorder
370688.statement:
Let $\mathcal{M}_n$ be the set of the labelled perfect matchings under consideration, and let $\preceq$ be the preorder on this set. A **switch** is the local transformation defined earlier in the paper. **Switch-generation conjecture.** If $N,M\in\mathcal{M}_n$ satisfy $N\preceq M$, then there exists a sequence

$$
N=M_1\preceq M_2\preceq\dots\preceq M_{k-1}\preceq M_k=M
$$

such that $M_j$ is a switch of $M_{j+1}$ for every $j$. This is presented as an open conjecture about whether the preorder is generated by switches; the supplied parser gives no evidence of resolution.

370836.title: Completeness conjecture for the Bollobás–Riordan polynomial of lens-space Heegaard graphs
370836.statement:
For a lens space $L(p,q)$, let $G_{p,q}$ denote its Heegaard graph, and let $R_{G_{p,q}}$ be the Bollobás–Riordan polynomial of that graph. Two lens spaces are homeomorphic exactly when their Heegaard graphs have the corresponding homeomorphism-class parameters.

**Bollobás–Riordan completeness conjecture.** The Bollobás–Riordan polynomial of the Heegaard graph of lens spaces is a complete invariant for lens spaces.

The Bollobás–Riordan polynomial specializes to the Tutte polynomial and therefore records richer embedding information. Computed exponent patterns distinguish the orbits $\{\pm q^{\pm1}\}$, but completeness for all lens spaces remains open.

370885.title: NP-hardness conjecture for sandwich problems with forbidden trees and cliques
370885.statement: For a set $\mathcal T$ of trees, a graph is $(\mathcal T\cup\{K_k\})$-free if it contains no member of $\mathcal T$ and no copy of $K_k$ as an induced subgraph. **Sandwich-problem hardness conjecture.** For every positive integer $k\geq 4$ and every possibly infinite set $\mathcal T$ of non-star trees, the sandwich problem for $(\mathcal T\cup\{K_k\})$-free graphs is NP-hard. This claim is presented as a consequence of the Gyárfás–Sumner and Brakensiek–Guruswami conjectures, so its status is unresolved when those conjectures are unresolved.

370940.title: Tokushige's conjecture on non-uniform cross-t-intersecting families
370940.statement:
Let $k\geq l\geq t\geq1$ and $n\geq(t+1)(k-t+1)$. Two families $\mathcal{A}\subseteq\binom{[n]}{k}$ and $\mathcal{B}\subseteq\binom{[n]}{l}$ are **cross-$t$-intersecting** if $|A\cap B|\geq t$ for every $A\in\mathcal{A}$ and $B\in\mathcal{B}$. **Tokushige's conjecture.** Then

$$
|\mathcal{A}||\mathcal{B}|\leq\binom{n-t}{k-t}\binom{n-t}{l-t}.
$$

This is presented as a conjecture for non-uniform cross-$t$-intersecting families, and the supplied text gives no resolution status.

371070.title: The b-chromatic number inequality for powers of Cartesian graph products
371070.statement:
Let $G$ and $H$ be graphs, let $k\text{?}$ be a positive integer, and write $\varphi$ for the $b$-chromatic number and $G^k$ for the $k$-th graph power. **Cartesian-product power conjecture.** For all graphs $G$ and $H$ and all $k\in\mathbb{N}$,

$$
\varphi((G\square H)^k)\geq\varphi(G^k\square H^k).
$$

The supplied text presents this inequality as a conjecture, and gives no evidence that it has been resolved.

371181.title: The first friendly-versus-antagonistic discrepancy outside the consecutive-ratio family
371181.statement:
Let $S=\{s_2,s_1\}$ with $s_2<s_1<2s_2$, and suppose

$$
\frac{s_1}{s_2}\neq\frac{k+1}{k}
$$

for every $k\in\mathbb{N}$. Let FvF and AvA denote the symmetric friendly and antagonistic self-interest games. **First-discrepancy conjecture.** There exists a heap with a friendly/antagonistic discrepancy, and the first such heap is

$$
x=(i+2)s_2+iks_1,
$$

where $i\in\mathbb{N}$ satisfies

$$
\frac{i+1}{i}>\frac{s_1}{s_2}>\frac{i+2}{k+i}.
$$

This conjecture complements the claimed no-discrepancy family above and is supported by the paper's analysis; it remains unresolved in the supplied text.

371255.title: High-connectivity conjecture for completability and hyperconnectivity
371255.statement:
Let $d$ be a positive integer, and let $G$ be a graph on $n$ vertices. Write ${\mathcal{S}}_d(G)$ and ${\mathcal{H}}_d(G)$ for the completability and hyperconnectivity matroids in dimension $d$, respectively. **High-connectivity conjecture.** For every positive integer $d$, there exists a positive integer $k_d$ such that every $k_d$-connected graph $G$ on $n$ vertices satisfies

$$
\operatorname{rank} {\mathcal{S}}_d(G) \geq dn-d^2
$$

and

$$
\operatorname{rank} {\mathcal{H}}_d(G) \geq dn-d^2.
$$

This would extend the paper's main theorem from bipartite rigidity to completability and hyperconnectivity for highly connected graphs. The supplied text gives no resolution, and the conjecture remains open.
